chunks: Abān ibn ʿUthmān narrated from ʿĪsā al-Qummī, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “I shoot an arrow, but I do not know whether I mentioned the Name of Allah or did not mention it.” So he said: “Eat, and there is no harm.”

I said: “I shoot, and it disappears from my sight, then I find my arrow in it.” He said: “Eat as long as nothing has been eaten from it; but if something has been eaten from it, then do not eat from it.”

key_terms.أَرْمِي: I shoot; referring here to hunting by shooting an arrow
key_terms.أَسَمَّيْتُ: I mentioned the Name of Allah; referring to tasmiyah at the time of shooting
key_terms.بِسَهْمٍ: with an arrow; the hunting instrument mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.كُلْ: eat; an expression of permissibility in this context
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; indicating permissibility
key_terms.يَغِيبُ: it disappears; meaning the hunted animal goes out of sight
key_terms.يُؤْكَلْ: is eaten from; meaning that a predator or other creature has eaten part of it

ai.seo_question: Can hunted game be eaten if I am unsure whether I mentioned Allah’s Name or if the animal disappeared before I found it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on hunted game struck by an arrow. It indicates permissibility when one is uncertain about having pronounced the tasmiyah, and it also permits eating game found later with one’s arrow in it so long as no animal has eaten from it.
